reviewNote: Drafted by Claude from the chart for faculty review. Not validated teaching content.
summary: VATS lobectomy for neuroendocrine lung cancer in a patient neurology thinks has Lambert-Eaton syndrome (needed a second sugammadex dose after EBUS), with marginal predicted postoperative lung function.

asa.rationale: COPD with ppoFEV1 44% and ppoDLCO 40%, suspected paraneoplastic LEMS.

decision.rationale: Cancer surgery should not wait weeks, but the team must plan for LEMS: minimize or avoid neuromuscular blockers, quantitative monitoring, ICU bed, and readiness for postoperative ventilation. Inform neurology; consider amifampridine.

redFlags.evidence: Neurology 10/13: proximal weakness, areflexia with post exercise facilitation, autonomic symptoms with LCNEC; VGCC antibody pending; EBUS 09/2026: weakness, diplopia, needed a second sugammadex dose.
redFlags.implication: Marked sensitivity to nondepolarizing and depolarizing blockers; prolonged weakness and respiratory failure.
redFlags.action: Avoid or minimize NMB (DLT under deep propofol and remifentanil, or small rocuronium dose), quantitative TOF, sugammadex, plan for postop ventilation, ICU.

redFlags.evidence: FEV1 52%, DLCO 48%, ppoFEV1 44%, ppoDLCO 40%, VO2 peak 15.8; emphysema; PaO2 71.
redFlags.implication: Hypoxemia on one lung ventilation and postoperative respiratory failure.
redFlags.action: Lung protective OLV, CPAP to the operative lung if needed, excellent analgesia, early mobilization.

redFlags.evidence: Thoracic epidural vs PVB or ESP per DOS team; aspirin held.
redFlags.action: Thoracic epidural or paravertebral block with multimodal adjuncts.

redFlags.implication: Not related to iodine or contrast.

planItems.item: Cefazolin 2 g within 60 min of incision
ICU or step down with ventilator backup

boothComplications.why: COPD with airway instrumentation by a DLT
